analyst_view.overall: PSG are top of the league phase with 12 points from 4 games and come off a 3-2 win at Nice on Saturday, while Roma are 20th with 4 points after losing 3-2 at Manchester United, though they are third and unbeaten in Serie A. PSG lost Desire Doue to what looked like a serious right knee injury at Nice (stretchered off, no contact), and Kvaratskhelia is out for months with a torn ACL; the numbers list no PSG absentees, so neither is taken off, but Kvara has been out since 20 October, so the recent form the numbers use already plays without him. Dembele, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Akliouche were all cleared to return before Nice, and Dembele came off the bench there. Roma get goalkeeper Svilar and Dybala back after injuries, while Rensch (adductor) and Pellegrini (thigh) stay out. No referee is named yet; the numbers already count both sides' recent form, which has been high-scoring.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, already lifted by both teams' scoring form (about +6% PSG, +4% Roma). I lean slightly lower, to about 3.6: Doue, one of PSG's main attackers, went off at Nice with a knee injury the numbers don't know about, and Roma have first-choice keeper Svilar back. Dembele's return limits how much PSG lose, so it stays a mild lean.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, with Roma's busy recent corner count already adding about 3%. PSG will have most of the ball and Gasperini's Roma attack wide with wing-backs, but nothing in the team news changes how many corners either side wins, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already trimmed for both sides' quiet recent card counts (PSG only 4 in their last 6). Roma's man-to-man pressing tends to draw fouls against a side that keeps the ball like PSG, which is why their share is the larger one; with no referee named yet and no derby or suspension angle, I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, with Roma's high recent shot count already adding about 17% to their side. Losing Doue costs PSG a shooter, but Dembele is back to take that role and PSG will still dominate the ball at home, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.9 shots on target, pushed up by PSG's very accurate recent run (60 on target in 6, +19%). I trim it slightly to about 12.4: Doue's injury removes one of PSG's sharpest finishers, and Roma's defence has been tighter in Serie A (unbeaten, third) than in Europe. A small lean because PSG's attack, with Dembele back, is still deep.
